abstract: Abstract One-third of deals in the venture capital (VC) market involve a founder and investor from the same university. Venture capitalists are more likely to invest in and place larger bets on startups with founders from their alma mater. These deals are also more likely to lead to IPOs postfunding. Tests using VC partner turnover confirm a direct link between education ties and funding likelihood. Taken together, our results suggest that university connections facilitate improved deal-making and outcomes, rather than diverting funds toward lower-quality startups.
journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
title: Alumni Networks in Venture Capital Financing

abstract: Drawing from the cognitive appraisal theory of emotions, this study hypothesizes and comparatively tests the effects of empathetic management and cultural intelligence on employee attitudes and behaviours in international business settings. Using a cross-sectional survey design, data were collected from 257 employees at a major U.S. motor coach company serving international clients (response rate: 59.21%). The asymptotically unbiased PLSF-SEM method was employed to test the theoretical model. Results demonstrate that empathetic management has significantly stronger positive effects than cultural intelligence on job satisfaction, job innovativeness, and likelihood of above-average job performance. The model explained 63% of the variance in job performance. The total effect of empathetic management on job performance was significantly greater than that of cultural intelligence. This study contributes to international business literature by providing empirical evidence that managerial empathy outperforms cultural intelligence in driving employee performance in multicultural work environments. Practically, organizations should prioritize developing empathetic management capabilities alongside cultural intelligence training. The findings suggest organizations should allocate greater resources to empathy training for managers while maintaining cultural intelligence development, particularly in service industries with diverse workforces.
title: The comparative effect of empathetic management and cultural intelligence on job performance: an empirical study of a company that serves international clients
